title: Import KML and KMZ and verify the resulting regions
summary: Import two fictional geospatial sources, diagnose an empty-file failure, and verify retained geometry, region flags and call search results.
prerequisites: A separate fictional practice map and access to Custom Maps, layer creation and imports.
The retained fictional KML/KMZ fixtures under demo/assets; review any operational source before importing.

scenes.title: Prepare a dedicated import layer
required_labels: TRAINING ONLY - KML and KMZ import
scenes.narration: Prepare a separate layer for the import exercise. Enter K M L and K M Z import as the Layer Name, set Order to twenty, choose Data Layer, and select Add Layer. The returned row shows the new layer with no image. This keeps the imported geometry separate from the existing ground-floor drawing and the earlier Geo J S O N example.
scenes.capture_intent: Show the actual target/file control, import history result, retained geometry or returned search option being discussed.

scenes.title: Select the map, target layer and KML file
required_labels: TRAINING ONLY - KML and KMZ import
scenes.narration: On Custom Maps, select Import for the Community coordination centre. In Import Geospatial Data, select the dedicated Target Layer. Choose the fictional assembly-area K M L file, review the target again and select Import. The file contains one named polygon. The source files for this exercise are retained with the Academy so the example can be reproduced.
scenes.practice: Select the map, target layer and KML file
scenes.capture_intent: Show the actual target/file control, import history result, retained geometry or returned search option being discussed.

scenes.title: Review history and repeat with KMZ
scenes.narration: Import History now shows import dot K M L, Type K M L, and Complete. The returned form has reset its target selection, so choose the dedicated layer again before the next upload. Choose the access-area K M Z archive and import it. History now contains separate Complete entries for K M L and K M Z. A completed import still needs a visual geometry review.

scenes.capture_intent: Show the actual target/file control, import history result, retained geometry or returned search option being discussed.

scenes.title: Read an import failure instead of assuming success
required_labels: No placemarks with a point, line or polygon were found in the file.
scenes.narration: This additional test selects the same target and uploads a K M L file with no placemarks. Its returned history row says Failed. The Error column explains that no placemarks with a point, line or polygon were found. Check the specific result and error for the intended run. Do not treat returning to the form as proof that useful geometry was imported.
scenes.practice: Read an import failure instead of assuming success
scenes.capture_intent: Show the actual target/file control, import history result, retained geometry or returned search option being discussed.

scenes.title: Inspect the actual retained polygons and their flags
scenes.narration: Open Region Editor for the dedicated layer. The two successful imports are visible as separate polygons and named entries. Select each polygon to review Region Properties. Both imported areas are Custom regions; Searchable in dispatch and Dispatchable are checked in this example. Review those defaults before operational use. The import status describes processing, while the map and properties show what was actually retained.
scenes.practice: Inspect the actual retained polygons and their flags
scenes.capture_intent: Show the actual target/file control, import history result, retained geometry or returned search option being discussed.

scenes.title: Verify search availability and apply the pattern
scenes.narration: On New Call, open Indoor Location and search for training. Both imported areas now appear as selectable results. No call is dispatched in this exercise. This pattern can bring reviewed planning areas into a search-and-rescue, security, wildland, industrial or community response department, alongside fire and E M S. Verify coordinates, naming and operational permissions before relying on imported reference data.
